analysis_notes.gap_analysis_detail: Torah #102 is a fragmentary teaching — the narrator explicitly states he did not merit to hear the full Torah ('לֹא זָכִיתִי לְשָׁמְעָהּ'). Only two bechina statements were recorded: (1) בֹּעַז הוּא בְּחִינַת גּוֹאֵל, (2) רוּת הִיא בְּחִינַת תְּפִלָּה. Both pairs are fully captured in the dataset. The source text also references דָּוִד and שִׁירוֹת וְתִשְׁבָּחוֹת, but these appear as explanatory intermediaries (the reason Ruth=תפלה, via the etymology of her name in the Gemara Berakhot 7b), not as independent bechina declarations. They are eitza-type bridges, not bechina nodes. The second section of the text (lines 3–4) about the Rebbe's hidden attainments vs. revealed words contains no bechina language and introduces no new nodes. No missing nodes identified.
analysis_notes.merge_decision_notes: Package 1 (גאולה/בעז) and Package 2 (תפלה/רות) are deliberately kept separate. The Torah's core concept is 'סוֹד סְמִיכַת גְּאֻלָּה לִתְפִלָּה' — the secret of JOINING redemption TO prayer. This 'joining' is an eitza (flow) relationship: redemption flows into/precedes prayer (as in the halakhic ruling of semikhat geulah la-tefillah). Redemption and prayer are distinct domains linked causally, not two expressions of the same essential nature. There is no bechina edge between the two pairs in the dataset, which correctly reflects this distinction.
